scope: Standing government and residential wings of Piratini Palace and the open court in Porto Alegre.
siteApproach: The 22-corner exterior and four-corner court reproduce the named relation. Positive Z faces Praça Marechal Deodoro. Original source ground falls from the plaza toward the rear and toward the east side of the façade.

sources.use: Primary restoration text describes the monumental stone portico, doubled center columns, Landowski statues flanking the main entrance, state shield, Doric frieze, balustrade and large glazed upper openings.
The written 2022 government inspection gives the current four-level government wing, three-level residential wing, their roof terraces and their footprint areas.
The owner attributes the project to Maurice Gras and separate façade sculptures to Paul Landowski. The written history identifies the government and residential wings.

imageryScreen.firstConsulted: The local Qualla image inventory and the linked native Commons record.

omitted.reason: Interior lounge and unknown original rights holder. The native file records assumed rather than confirmed authorship.

imageryScreen.candidates: Review the exact original 1922 Maurice Gras published drawing and the 1921 government report photograph. Use the standing outline and public works facts to account for later changes.
imageryScreen.selected: Written restoration and site inspection only. Started with the published Qualla files. Negrinho.jpg is an interior view with assumed authorship. Other available published media depict historic paintings unrelated to the current exterior or require attribution. The original published rendition of the 1921 and 1922 exterior views was unavailable to verify. The model uses the restoration and building survey text, original boundary, and elevation.
